raw_case_text:
A 38 years old female presented to the physician 2 days after receiving a viral vector COVID-19 vaccine. She developed myalgia, fever and skin rash and visited to a medical center. Her vital signs were as the followings: body temperature 38.5 C, blood pressure 120/80 mm Hg, pulse rate 85/min and respiratory rate 16/min. The diagnostic workup showed decreased platelet count (80 x 103/microL). This case was firstly suspicious for a possible vaccine adverse reaction. Nevertheless, there is no coagulation profile abnormality. Since the setting is a tropical country that viral hemorrhagic disease is common, further investigation for viral hemorrhagic disease was performed. Further laboratory tests confirm that there is a positive result of dengue virus infection (Dengue NS1Ag + ve). The final diagnosis in this case is dengue. The patient receipt standard fluid replacement therapy. All of her clinical problems, including skin rash, disappeared within 1 week.
This is a case of dengue hemorrhagic fever that occurs in a patient who has just received COVID-19 vaccination for 2 days. It is a possible condition that might occur in any tropical country during the current worldwide mass vaccination. It is necessary to recognize an endemic hemorrhagic fever that might cause thrombocytopenia in a COVID-19 vaccine recipient. This clinical problem might be missed diagnosed as an adverse event of vaccine. A coincidence of fever following COVID-19 vaccine and endemic tropical disease is a possible emerging problem in the present day. The present case is a good example and practitioner should aware of this scenario when dealing with post-vaccination thrombocytopenia problem.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old female presented with acute myalgia, fever, and skin rash beginning 2 days after receiving a viral-vector COVID-19 vaccine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two days after receiving a viral-vector COVID-19 vaccination in a tropical dengue-endemic country, the patient developed acute fever, myalgia, and a cutaneous rash, prompting evaluation for suspected vaccine-induced adverse reaction versus endemic viral hemorrhagic fever.
subjective.past_medical_history: Received viral-vector COVID-19 vaccine 2 days prior to symptom onset; resident of a tropical dengue-endemic region.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, myalgia, and skin rash.

objective.physical_examination: Body temperature 38.5 C, blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate 85/min, respiratory rate 16/min, and cutaneous rash.
objective.routine_investigations: Thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 80 x 10^3/uL and a normal coagulation profile.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Acute dengue fever/dengue hemorrhagic fever coincidentally presenting 2 days after viral-vector COVID-19 vaccination (excluding vaccine-induced prothrombotic immune thrombocytopenia), confirmed by positive dengue NS1 antigen testing and normal coagulation parameters. Treated with standard fluid replacement therapy, with complete resolution of fever, rash, and thrombocytopenia within 1 week.
